title: The regular integral coefficient module is the limit of its concrete residue modules
statement: For any scheme X and prime l, let R_X=p_X^*continuousMapRingObj(Z_l) [def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring]. Define q_n:R_X->C(-,Z/l^n) as the canonical condensed-to-continuous chartComparison of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] followed by the actual continuous reduction toZModPow n. Regard C(-,Z/l^n) [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-regular-functions] as an R_X-module by restriction along q_n, with transitions the usual residue reductions. The cone of q_n with vertex regular R_X is a limit cone in internal R_X-modules. This includes n=0, where Z/l^0 is the zero ring. No invertibility or finiteness hypothesis on X is required.

proof.text: The concrete residue ring is the sheaf of continuous Z/l^n-valued functions. Define its R_X action through chartComparison followed by PadicInt.toZModPow, and define transitions by ZMod.castHom. Tensor naturality proves their linearity, and castHom_toZModPow_succ proves compatibility. Thus the actual regular R_X-module is the vertex of a specified cone, including n=0.

On every topological space S, a compatible system of continuous maps S->Z/l^n lifts pointwise by PadicInt.ofCompatible. For continuity at x and epsilon>0, choose n with l^(-n)<epsilon. The open fiber of the nth residue through x makes differences have zero nth residue; ker_toZModPow and norm_le_pow_iff_mem_span_pow bound their norms by l^(-n). The residue maps determine a p-adic integer uniquely. Therefore continuous Z_l-valued functions are the sectionwise inverse limit.

The canonical chartComparison is an isomorphism for Z_l, using its ultrametric totally disconnected topology. Transfer the sectionwise limiting cone across this specified isomorphism. The sheaf-to-presheaf and module forgetful functors reflect limits; naturality of the explicit module transition maps identifies the underlying diagram with the continuous residue diagram. This proves Nonempty(IsLimit(tateResidueModuleCone X l)).
